chunks: We said: What we say is that the existence of the Imam with authority (Manbast al-Yad), if it is established that he is a grace upon us according to what we have demonstrated, and his creation is not within our power, it would not be fitting that we be required to create him, for it would be a duty that is beyond capacity.

And empowering his hand and strengthening his authority may be within our capacity and within the capacity of Allah. So when Allah does not do that, we know that it is not obligatory upon Him, but that it is obligatory upon us.
Because he must be one with authority for the purpose of the duty to be realized.

And we explained by this that if empowering his hand were from His action, He would compel the creation to it. And His intervening between him and his enemies, and strengthening his command through the angels, might lead to the falling away of the purpose of the duty and the occurrence of compulsion.
Therefore, it is obligatory upon us to empower him in every condition, and if we do not do so, it is from ourselves.
ai.seo_question: What is the theological distinction between the creation of the Imam and the empowerment of his authority in Shia thought?
ai.summary: This passage from Al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* articulates the Shia doctrine of *Bast al-Yad* (extending the hand), distinguishing between the divine creation of the Imam and the human obligation to actively support his political authority. It posits that if God were to unilaterally enforce the Imam’s rule, it would negate human free will and the test of faith; thus, believers must exert effort to establish his governance to fulfill the purpose of divine command.
